To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the greater absolute depressor response to ICV GABAA agonist is due to a higher baseline blood pressure in the SHR, not to differences in the number or affinity of GABA receptors.

the total sympathetic nervous system contribution (i.e., ganglionic blockade) to arterial pressure is equivalent in the SHR and WKY, but that the GABAergic system is more effective in the SH rat in producing a depressor response.

intraventricular GABA produces a greater absolute depressor response in spontaneously hypertensive rats than in age matched normotensive rats and this effect is not due to differences in the number or binding affinity of GABA receptors in the forebrain or pons-medullary brain regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of GABA in the central control of blood pressure.
the role of the sympathetic nervous system in hypertension and the role of GABA in the control of blood pressure.
the role of central GABAergic mechanisms in the pathogenesis of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the greater absolute depressor effects produced by GABA in SH compared to WKY rats is not due to differences in either GABA receptor binding characteristics or in the functional contribution of the sympathetic nervous system to blood pressure.

GABA receptors in the forebrain and cerebellum do not appear to play a role in the pathogenesis of spontaneous hypertension in the SH rat, and that the greater absolute depressor response to ICV GABAA is not due to a difference in GABA receptor density in the brain.

the GABA system in the brain of adult SH rats is not different from WKY rats in terms of GABA binding characteristics, GABA-mediated cardiovascular effects and the GABA-mediated cardiovascular response to ganglionic blockade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the greater absolute depressor response to GABA in the SHR compared with the WKY does not appear to result from a greater GABA receptor sensitivity in the SHR.
the greater absolute depressor response to central GABA is not related to a difference in GABA receptor number or binding affinity in the brain of the SH compared to the WKy rat.
the greater depressor response of the SHR to central GABA is not mediated by a difference in the GABA receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the depressor effect of central GABA is greater in SHR compared to WKY rats and this is not due to differences in central GABA receptor binding characteristics.

the greater absolute depressor response of GABA in SH rats is not due to a change in GABA receptor affinity or density, but rather to a greater functional contribution of the central GABAergic system in SH rats.
there are no major differences in GABAergic tone or GABA receptor binding between the two strains of rats.
